# INTRODUCTION {background-image="latar.png" background-opacity=".75"}

::: notes
Good morning everyone. Let me start with the background of this project.

Every day, the DTA team creates delivery routes for transporters. These
transporters deliver finished products to the customers of PT XYZ who
have placed orders.

Right now, this process is still done manually. Because of that, it
takes a long time, and we are never sure if the routes are really the
best ones.

So, the DTA team wants to build an optimization model to solve this
problem.
:::

## Objective {.center}

::: notes
This slide shows the goal of the project.

Our goal is to build an optimization model that finds the best routes
for the transporters, with the lowest total cost.

The model needs to answer three simple questions. First, which customer
order should we deliver? Second, on which date? And third, which
vehicle should we use? After that, the model also decides the order of
the deliveries.
:::

Build a *transporter* routing optimization model that minimizes *total cost*, by creating a configuration of:

> **Which _Customer_ orders should be delivered on which date and using which fleet. Then determine the delivery sequence!**


# *Business Process* {background-image="armada.png" background-opacity=".75"}

::: notes
Now, let me explain the business process.

We deliver products from two warehouses: Ciawi and Cibitung. To do
this, the DTA team rents transporters with many types of vehicles.

Each vehicle type is different. It has a maximum volume it can carry,
a maximum weight it can carry, a rental cost per kilometer, and a
loading time. For this model, we assume the rental cost is fixed. It
does not change because of the driver or the route.

Also, each vehicle type has limits. We can only rent a certain number
of vehicles, and each vehicle can only visit a certain number of
customers in one trip.
:::

## *Purchase Order* {.smaller .center}

Customers order (through a *purchase order* - PO process) a number of
finished products from **PT XYZ**. From the PO, we have the following
information:

1.  The total cubic volume and tonnage of products to be delivered.
2.  The delivery date *range* of the products.

**PT XYZ** must fulfill the purchase directly (splitting the delivery
of products in one PO into several deliveries is not allowed). Each
customer will be served by either the Ciawi or Cibitung warehouse
according to a predetermined allocation. No customer is served by
both.

::: notes
This slide is about the purchase order, or PO.

Customers order products from PT XYZ through a purchase order. From
each PO, we know two things: how much volume and weight we need to
deliver, and the range of dates when we can deliver it.

There are two important rules here. First, one PO must be delivered in
one trip. We cannot split it into several deliveries. Second, each
customer is served by only one warehouse, either Ciawi or Cibitung.
This is already decided before, so no customer is served by both.
:::

# Fleet Restrictions at Customers {background-image="retail.png" background-opacity=".75"}

::: notes
Next, there is one more restriction, and it comes from the customer
side.

Not all vehicles can reach all customers. Some customers are located
on big roads, so large trucks can go there safely. But some customers
are in small streets, so only small vehicles can reach them.

So, the model must also respect this rule when it chooses a vehicle
for each customer.
:::

::: notes
Now, let me show you the data that we use in this model. There are
four datasets: customer orders, customer details, warehouse data, and
fleet data.
:::


# Optimization Goal

::: notes
Now, let me explain the optimization model itself: what it decides,
and what it tries to achieve.
:::

## _Decision Variables_ {.center}

This optimization model produces the following _decision variables_:

1. Delivery date,
1. Fleet used, and
1. Delivery sequence.

For each _customer sales order_.

::: notes
These are the decision variables. In simple words, this is the output
of the model.

For every customer order, the model decides three things: the delivery
date, the vehicle to use, and the sequence of the deliveries in each
trip.
:::

## _Objective Function_ {.center}

The objective function of this model is:

> Minimize the total cost arising from every decision of _customer_ $i$ being delivered by fleet $j$ on date $k$ without violating the existing _constraints_.

::: notes
And this is the objective function.

The model tries to minimize the total cost. Every decision has a cost:
sending customer i, using vehicle j, on date k. The model picks the
combination with the lowest total cost.

Of course, it must follow all the rules we talked about before: the
vehicle capacity, the delivery time window, and the fleet restrictions
at each customer.
:::
